pages.text: $(l)Avoid level emitters for automation triggers$()$(li)Level emitters rebuild the entire crafting cache on any grid change, causing quadratic lag in large networks
$(li)Instead, use OpenComputers scripts (e.g., AE2 AutoStock) to manage stockpiling via direct pattern requests

$(l)Use OpenComputers for crafting monitoring and automation$()$(li)OC cannot directly read AE2 crafting job status beyond idle/busy$(li)Infer completion by requesting a craftable item and checking the $(5)requesting()$() count of the returned $(5)CraftingStatus$() object

$(l)Handle extended crafting recipes via PackagedAuto$()$(li)Encode multi-grid recipes (e.g., 5×5+) using a Recipe Package Encoder into Package Recipe Holders$(li)Place one holder in a Packager linked to your ME system

$(li)Place the other in an Unpackager inside the group of Package Crafters (Advanced/Elite/Ultimate); underneath them it only feeds the bottom crafter$(li)The ME system will now craft the recipe on request without custom scripts

$(l)CPU targeting in AE2 is name-based only$()$(li)AE2’s API only supports whitelisting CPUs by name—no blacklisting$(li)Unnamed CPUs return an empty string for the name field, so only explicitly named CPUs can be targeted
$(li)Always name your OC CPUs before configuring AE2 integration
